_comment: Demonstrates THRIVE §6.5 DevelopmentalContext and §6.6 TemporalCycleProfile during a major life transition. The fundamental Max-Neef needs remain unchanged; only satisfiers and capacity baselines shift. See THRIVE §6.5 rule: stage modifies satisfiers, not needs.

context.name: Self Stewardship — Caregiving Transition
context.scope: Personal wellbeing, executive function, and caregiving coordination while operating a small business

developmental_context.life_stage: sandwich generation — primary caregiver for aging parent while running a business
developmental_context.current_focus_or_tension: Balancing business continuity with increased caregiving obligations; sleep and recovery are irregular but the need for connection and rest has not diminished — only how they are met has changed.

temporal_cycle_profile.label: Caregiving transition — irregular capacity
temporal_cycle_profile.approximate_period: months (estimated 6–18 months until care arrangements stabilize)
temporal_cycle_profile.capacity_effect: baseline reduction across cognitive, emotional, and recovery dimensions during low-capacity phases
high_capacity_phases: weekday mornings before 10am when parent is settled and no urgent business calls
Sunday afternoons when backup caregiver is available
low_capacity_phases: overnight and early morning when sleep is interrupted
days following medical appointments or care plan changes
end-of-quarter business deadlines overlapping with care escalations

capacity_profile._note: Reduced baselines reflect current load, not a judgment about capability. Capacity is expected to recover as care arrangements stabilize.

needs.label: Affection (Max-Neef)

satisfiers.prior_to_transition: Regular social time with close friends; weekly dinner with partner; informal check-ins with colleagues
satisfiers.current: Daily presence with parent during care routines; brief voice messages to friends instead of in-person visits; partner check-in during morning coffee before the day fragments

needs._note: The need for affection is unchanged. Satisfiers have shifted toward caregiving relationships and shorter, more frequent connection points.

needs.label: Leisure (Max-Neef)

satisfiers.prior_to_transition: Evening reading; weekend hikes; monthly live music events
satisfiers.current: 15-minute audiobook during parent's nap; one short neighborhood walk when backup is available; no live events until care schedule stabilizes

needs._note: Leisure need persists at the same priority. Scope of satisfiers has narrowed temporarily — this is a capacity adaptation, not a deprioritization of the need.

needs.label: Protection (Max-Neef)

satisfiers.prior_to_transition: Routine health checkups; stable income from business; home security and insurance review
satisfiers.current: Same health checkups maintained; business continuity plan activated with delegated client communication; added parent medication tracking and emergency contact list

needs._note: Protection need unchanged. Satisfiers expanded to include parent's safety without removing self-protection measures.

routines.label: Evening wind-down
steps: Set phone to do-not-disturb except care emergency contacts
Five minutes of stretching or breathing — no productivity expectations
Write one line in journal: what went okay today
known_failure_modes: parent needs assistance after bedtime routine starts
fallback_options: Skip journal; keep breathing exercise only
Defer wind-down to next available quiet window — no catch-up required

routines.label: Morning micro-reset
steps: Identify one essential task for the business day — not a full plan
Send one brief check-in message to backup caregiver or partner
fallback_options: Water only — reset rest of routine when a gap appears
Essential task can be as small as 'reply to one client email'

transition_notes: Declared 2026-06-01 when parent moved in following a fall. What changed: satisfiers for Affection and Leisure were reassigned to fit available time and energy; CapacityProfile baselines were reduced to match current load; two low-capacity routine overrides were activated. What did not change: the underlying Max-Neef needs, their relative priorities, or the steward's dignity. This transition is treated as a temporary capacity phase, not a permanent downgrade of wellbeing requirements.
